cards.front: Which sensory nerve runs along the medial leg? [___]
cards.context: It supplies sensation along the medial leg and foot. Because it is sensory, injury does not directly paralyse the quadriceps.

cards.front: The only bony connection between the upper limb and axial skeleton is the [___] joint.
cards.context: The medial clavicle sits in front of major vessels and the trachea. Posterior displacement can therefore threaten structures entering the chest.

cards.front: The synovial joint formed by tibia, fibula and talus is the [___] joint.
cards.context: This mortise joint transfers leg loads to the foot. Its bony shape makes dorsiflexion and plantarflexion the dominant movements.

cards.front: Which bone is lateral to the tibia? [___]
cards.context: The fibula contributes to ankle stability and provides muscle attachment. It is not the main bone transmitting body weight from knee to ankle.

cards.front: The plexus supplying the upper limb is formed mainly by roots [___].
cards.context: The brachial plexus is formed by the anterior rami of spinal nerves C5 through T1 before reorganising into trunks, divisions and cords.

reference.title: Anatomy, Head and Neck: Brachial Plexus - StatPearls

cards.front: The leg compartment that lifts the forefoot during swing is the [___] compartment.
cards.context: Dorsiflexors lift the forefoot during swing phase. Weakness allows the toes to catch the ground and may produce foot drop.

cards.front: Which nerve supplies the main muscles that extend the wrist? [___]
cards.context: Loss of these extensors can produce wrist drop. Localisation also depends on which finger movements and sensory territories are affected.

reference.title: Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Nerves - StatPearls

cards.front: Which girdle attaches each lower limb to the trunk skeleton? [___]
cards.context: The hip bones transfer load between the lower limbs and vertebral column. This differs from the freely hanging shoulder girdle.

reference.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology: The Pelvic Girdle and Pelvis
